scenario.name: CISA AA22-321A, Unit 42 & Sophos — Hunters International Ransomware: Hive Rust Lineage, SharpWMI Lateral Movement & COM IVssBackupComponents Shadow Deletion
scenario.overview: Imagine a high-ceiling logistics warehouse with towering steel pallet racks stacked with labeled shipping crates, clipboard dock stations, and a bright yellow forklift cruising down the aisle. Inside the bustling logistics warehouse, an unverified driver climbs into a parked yellow forklift and rolls toward the high-bay customer storage racks. In this real-world scenario, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the high-bay pallet racks & forklift, then smuggles copied records out past the loading dock check-out clipboards in tiny disguised batches. The warehouse barcode inventory system flashes an urgent alert when hundreds of customer pallets are relabeled in minutes outside normal shift hours. In this scenario (T1047, CISA AA22-321A, Unit 42 & Sophos, Hunters International Ransomware: Hive Rust Lineage, SharpWMI Lateral Movement & COM IVssBackupComponents Shadow Deletion), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: sharpWMI Remote Execution, then direct COM, then multi-Threaded Rust Encryption. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering SharpWMI Remote Execution, then Direct COM, then Multi-Threaded Rust Encryption, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact)
